provenance.how: TRANSCRIBED, not produced by bench_wfn_loader.py. These rows are the step-0 fold measurement and the step-1b promotion gate, copied from the artifacts named in `source` below. bench_wfn_loader.py is the driver that REGENERATES them; running it is a future bench invocation, not a test (charter: step 6 cites measured numbers).

jobs.56446562: step-0 fold measurement, 2026-08-07, `lx run --cpu -n 4`, CPU milan 2x2. BOTH arms driven through the SAME PhdfCtx, so a difference between them is the request shape and nothing else. Artifacts /pscratch/sd/j/jackm/svc_wfn_loader/_measure_fold/.
jobs.56456596: step-1b promotion gate: the same read AFTER the union read moved into SlabIO.read_slabs. Its job was to reproduce 56446562's union numbers -- any regression would have been a defect in the move.

provenance.mb_named: DERIVED per row as warm_min_s * mbps_warm_min, both of which the artifact records. It is the bytes the REQUEST names (sum over windows of prod(valid_shape) * 8), not the padded slab -- rating a read by its padding would make a raggeder deck look faster. CROSS-CHECK, and the reason it is trustworthy: the union and fold arms read identical bytes, and their independently-recorded (time, rate) pairs agree to 0.54% (gnppm 0-10), 0.06% (gnppm 0-82) and 0.01% (MoS2), and the MoS2 figure lands on the 15.6 GB the design brief states independently.
provenance.no_median: warm_s (median) is deliberately absent. The artifacts record a rep LIST and quote warm-MIN as the headline; inventing a median from 2-3 transcribed reps would add a number nobody measured. Comparing a median against a warm-min is exactly how the draft of docs/services/wfn_loader.md got a row wrong.

THE ROW THE RULING TURNS ON: only 1.44x here, but +2.1 s per psi load at P=4, of which ~1.4 s is per-call collective H5Dread overhead (144 x ~42.7 ms vs one union call) and ~0.6 s is the extra jnp.stack the union path never needs. The cost axis is n_windows = the request's IBZ k-count, which is exactly the axis production decks grow along -- so the gap widens, it does not close.
